title: Anderson Minor and the Lawrence Tucker Oriental Serenaders
summary: He played spot jobs and carnival parades with Anderson Minor, and recalls the lineup of the late-1920s Lawrence Tucker band, called the Oriental Serenaders.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. Drums. Who was the drums? The drum, Albert Jobs. Oh, yeah. What was that? Do you know where you played? You played in different places?
No, we played in different places. Spot jobs. All around dance halls, bunkers. Yeah.
Whose band was it? It was the band. It was the band. It was the band.
It was the band. It was the band. It was the band.
Oh, was that the Oriental Serenaders or something, did you call it?
That, that, that, what the name was, Oriental Serenaders. That's what it was called, huh? Yeah. Oriental's. Yeah. Well, where'd you get that name from?
I was, no, I found them with that man. Same place as she got their uniform. What, uh, you play the sort of, the same way as you're playing now, in those days or something?

Did you play a change or anything? I played the same way. Uh, me and Jack Teagarden, the white fella played at the Palace Theatre. We was the first one started playing, uh, solos on trombone. Yeah? Before Tommy Dawson. Really? Sure. Wasn't it, George? Yeah. The first one started playing solos on trombone. Jack Teagarden. Did I have Jack Teagarden? Sure. Yeah. We went to Vic Gasper together. To where? Vic Gasper. At, uh, the, uh, Trombone. Was Jack Teagarden from here? Jack Teagarden from Texas, but he used to live here.
Yeah? Yeah? I didn't know. Huh? That's something I didn't know. He's from Texas, but he used to live here.
